title: Injector Circuit/Open
plain: The engine computer found a problem in the fuel injector electrical circuits but hasn't pinned it to one cylinder.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough running or misfire
Hard starting or stalling
Poor fuel economy

causes.name: Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the injectors
Damaged or chafed injector wiring harness
Loose or corroded injector connector
Faulty fuel injector
Faulty injector driver in the engine computer

checks: Check for cylinder-specific injector codes and misfire codes
Check the injector fuse and power feed
Inspect the injector harness for rubbing, heat damage or rodent chewing
fix: Usually a wiring, fuse or connector repair. Replace an injector only after testing confirms it.

cost.job: Diagnose and repair injector circuit wiring

drive: Limit driving. A dead injector circuit causes misfires that can overheat the catalytic converter. If the check engine light flashes, the engine shakes, loses power or stalls, slow down and get it checked right away. If it runs smoothly, get it to a shop in the next few days.
test_first: Check the injector fuse and relay, then check power and the control signal at the injectors and inspect the harness for chafing before replacing injectors or the computer.

title: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 1
plain: The engine computer sees a problem in the wiring or electrical signal for the fuel injector on cylinder 1, so that cylinder may not be getting fuel.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough idle or shaking
Misfire or stumble, often with a cylinder 1 misfire code
Less power and worse fuel economy

causes.name: Faulty fuel injector on cylinder 1 (open or shorted coil)
Loose, damaged or corroded injector connector
Broken or chafed injector wire in the harness
Blown fuse or lost power feed to the injectors
Faulty injector driver inside the engine computer

checks: Look for a loose, broken or corroded connector at the cylinder 1 injector
Measure the injector's resistance and compare it with the other injectors
Use a noid light or scope to confirm the computer is pulsing the injector
fix: Usually a new cylinder 1 injector or a wiring or connector repair. The engine computer itself is rarely the cause.
drive: Limit driving. A dead cylinder 1 injector causes a misfire that can overheat the catalytic converter. If the check engine light flashes, the engine shakes, loses power or stalls, slow down and get it checked right away. If it runs smoothly, get it to a shop in the next few days.
test_first: Check the cylinder 1 injector connector and resistance, then check power and the control signal with a noid light or scope before replacing the injector or the computer.

title: Cylinder 1 Injection Timing
plain: The computer has detected that fuel is being injected into cylinder 1 at the wrong moment. This code mostly shows up on modern diesel and direct-injection engines.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough running, knocking or a misfire
Smoke from the exhaust or worse fuel economy

causes.name: Faulty or sticking injector on cylinder 1
Injector wiring or connector problem
Injector correction (trim) codes not programmed after injector replacement
Low or unstable fuel rail pressure
Engine computer software issue

checks: Fix any fuel pressure or injector circuit codes first
Inspect the cylinder 1 injector connector and wiring
If injectors were replaced recently, confirm their trim codes were programmed
fix: Most often a new injector for that cylinder, programmed to the engine computer, after wiring and fuel pressure problems are ruled out.

title: Cold Start Injector 1
plain: Some older engines used an extra injector to add fuel during cold starts. The computer sees a problem with cold start injector 1 or its wiring.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Hard starting when the engine is cold
Fuel smell or rough running if the injector leaks

causes.name: Faulty cold start injector
Damaged wiring or corroded connector
Faulty thermo-time switch that controls the injector
Engine computer fault

checks: Inspect the cold start injector connector and wiring
Measure the injector's resistance against the spec
Test the thermo-time switch if the engine has one
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new cold start injector.

title: Engine Shutoff Solenoid
plain: Many diesel engines use a solenoid to cut off fuel when you turn the key off. The computer sees a problem with that solenoid or its wiring.
symptoms: Engine won't start, or won't shut off with the key
Engine stalls or cuts out while driving
Check engine light on

causes.name: Faulty fuel shutoff solenoid
Damaged wiring or corroded connector
Blown fuse or bad relay
Engine computer fault

checks: Check the fuse and relay for the shutoff solenoid
Listen for the solenoid clicking when the key is turned on
Inspect the solenoid connector and wiring
fix: Usually a new shutoff solenoid or a wiring repair.

title: Injector/Injection Timing Control Circuit
plain: On diesel engines the computer controls exactly when fuel is injected. It sees a problem in the circuit that controls that timing.
symptoms: Hard starting
Rough running, stalling or loss of power
Extra smoke from the exhaust
Check engine light on

causes.name: Failing injection pump or its electronic driver
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the pump
Low fuel supply from a weak lift pump or clogged filter
Faulty injection timing sensor
Engine computer fault

checks: Check fuel supply pressure and the fuel filter first
Inspect the injection pump wiring and connectors
Check timing data on a scan tool while the engine runs
fix: Often a fuel supply repair or a new injection pump driver or pump. Confirm fuel supply is good before replacing the pump.
examples: Well known on GM 6.5L diesels with a failing pump-mounted fuel solenoid driver
Also seen on Dodge Ram Cummins trucks with the VP44 injection pump

title: Engine Coolant Over Temperature Condition
plain: The engine has gotten hotter than is safe. Driving while it overheats can quickly warp or crack major engine parts.
symptoms: Temperature gauge high or an overheating warning
Steam or a sweet coolant smell from under the hood
Engine may cut power to protect itself
Heater may blow cold air

causes.name: Low coolant from a leak
Cooling fan or fan relay not working
Thermostat stuck closed
Failing water pump
Clogged radiator
Blown head gasket
Faulty coolant temperature sensor

checks: Let the engine cool, then check the coolant level (never open a hot radiator cap)
Make sure the cooling fans run when the engine is hot or the AC is on
Have the cooling system pressure tested for leaks
fix: Depends on the cause: most often a coolant leak repair, a new thermostat, or a cooling fan repair. Stop driving until it's fixed.
drive: No. Pull over safely and shut the engine off as soon as you can; driving while overheating can warp the cylinder head or blow the head gasket. Let it cool before checking anything and never open a hot radiator cap. Have it towed unless a shop confirms it's safe to move.
test_first: Check coolant level and for leaks, confirm the fans run, and compare the sensor reading to actual temperature. Test the thermostat, water pump and head gasket before replacing parts.

title: Transmission Fluid Over Temperature Condition
plain: The transmission fluid has gotten too hot. Hot fluid breaks down fast and can damage the transmission.
symptoms: Transmission temperature or warning light on
Harsh shifting or slipping
Burning smell

causes.name: Heavy towing, hauling or hot weather driving
Low or burnt transmission fluid
Clogged transmission cooler or cooler lines
Internal slipping in the transmission or torque converter
Faulty transmission fluid temperature sensor

checks: Pull over and let the transmission cool
Check the fluid level and condition
Check the transmission cooler and lines for blockage or damage
fix: Often a fluid service and cooler repair. If the fluid is burnt or the transmission slips, it may need internal repair.
drive: Not safely for long. Pull over and let the transmission cool, and stop towing or hauling. If it slips, shifts harshly or smells burnt, don't keep driving; heat breaks down the fluid fast and can ruin the transmission. Have it checked before driving far or in hot weather.
test_first: Check transmission fluid level and condition, confirm actual fluid temperature on a scan tool, and inspect the cooler and lines for restriction before replacing the sensor or transmission.

title: Engine Overspeed Condition
plain: The engine spun faster than its safe maximum speed at some point. The computer logs this because over-revving can damage the engine.
symptoms: Check engine light on
You may have noticed the engine revving very high
Often no other symptoms afterward

causes.name: Downshifting a manual transmission into too low a gear
Slipping transmission or clutch letting the engine flare
Erratic crankshaft position sensor signal
Engine computer fault

checks: Think back to any missed shift or sudden high-rev moment
Check the transmission fluid and watch for slipping
Inspect the crankshaft position sensor wiring
fix: If it came from a missed shift, clear the code and listen for new engine noises. If it comes back on its own, check for a slipping transmission or clutch.

title: Cylinder 7 Injection Timing
plain: The computer has detected that fuel is being injected into cylinder 7 at the wrong moment. This code mostly shows up on modern diesel and direct-injection engines.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough running, knocking or a misfire
Smoke from the exhaust or worse fuel economy

causes.name: Faulty or sticking injector on cylinder 7
Injector wiring or connector problem
Injector correction (trim) codes not programmed after injector replacement
Low or unstable fuel rail pressure
Engine computer software issue

checks: Fix any fuel pressure or injector circuit codes first
Inspect the cylinder 7 injector connector and wiring
If injectors were replaced recently, confirm their trim codes were programmed
fix: Most often a new injector for that cylinder, programmed to the engine computer, after wiring and fuel pressure problems are ruled out.
